$GRAB

Grab had an exceptional Q3.

- $1.12B of revenue, the first billion dollar quarter
- 57M monthly users, fastest QoQ growth since 2022
- EBITDA margins now highest in history of the company at 21%, up 565 basis points YoY
- Raised EBITDA guide from 45% growth to 60% growth YoY
- Total quarterly active advertisers on self-serve platform grew 39% YoY, and average spend of these advertisers grew 13% YoY
- Adjusted FCF now $533M, doubling YoY
- Financial services is now profitable
- Bought back $400M of stock, CEO bought $30M himself.

11B marketcap, 5B in cash, doing $4.2B of revenue and growing the bottom line 60%.

Listening to the call, looks like Meta chose Grab to be one of the first partners to integrate with Muse in Singapore. It is not easy for a company to do $1B in revenue every 90 days and it is also not easy to have 7% of the entire SEA population using your products, while growing that number 20% YoY. Network effects compounding with operating leverage is the simple thesis, unfortunately oil has been the headwind but this was an outstanding quarter for the company.

text:
Just finished with the $BDSX call, not a great result. Did 24% volume growth which is good, but test mix between Nodify XL2 and Nodify CDT lead to lower overall ASPs and that sounds like the new normal.

Combined with no service revenue for the quarter (basically consulting) you end up a couple million in rev short of consensus (around 10%). You def don't want to miss in this tape, and it pushes out the story a lot.

The acquisition thesis is still live and well in my mind (maybe moreso with a distressed company) as the product is just as important as it was yesterday, but who knows how management feels about that at lower prices. It makes negotiating trickier.

I did trim a bit that i bought going into earnings today as I don't want to get completely rekt, but maybe shouldn't have gone so risk on given the general environment.

referenced.text:
Was pretty consistent selling in $BDSX Friday, i increased to 12.2% which is about as high as i can make a position (actually this is irresponsibly long, lets be honest, though I am also mentally prepared for a 0 on the entire position, so maybe not).

I guess we are just going to see who is right and who is not right on this one but momentum clearly in control atm. That said, given the distribution of outcomes here and my thesis, i find it hard not to believe Kelly Criterion > Sharpe.

-We are talking 2.63x gross profit
-i think we see 23-24% growth when they report November 5th.
-There is a very credible acquisition thesis (strategically important to multiple buyers as BDSX's tech is increasingly important as multicancer screening increases (more multicancer screening = more lung nodules detected = more stratifying the risk of those nodules).
-We're also well below where Schuler (huge insider) was buying in August now ($24.50).

The next interesting information to come up will be in November when Gary Pestano, Chief Scientific Officer, speaks about MRD November 11 “Listening for the Whisper - Monitoring Residual Disease and Emerging Resistance in the Blood”. Pestano worked at Ventana which was another huge Schuler investment (flipped to Roche Diagnostics for 3b, Schuler made 300m). Now he’s Chief Science Officer at BDSX? I dunno, seems like the team is working to get the best possible result here, and over a very very long period of time.

The price action says something is up - but we're not talking about a big company here (223m market cap with half the float owned by insiders) so the PA is less trustworthy (there’s no fund with 50m of this and a full time analyst sweating it non stop).

This ticks all my boxes for an investment, so 🤷‍♂️... my fate awaits.

It's really tempting for me to be defensive since my year has still been very good, even after Thursday (i entered with 20% of my portfolio as compute which pretty aggressively nuked though Friday bounced at least a little), but i guess i just have to continuously tell myself to make decisions that lead to maximizing the amount of EV / money i make. There are a lot of incentives to not do that, but ultimately it is the only thing that matters for me personally.

Nothing in this post is financial advice or a suggestion to buy $BDSX, i am just clarifying my own thought process around a large holding of mine and thought others might find this entertaining - as i mentioned, i'm also extremely aware that this company could cause permanent capital loss.

Nothing in this thread is investing advice or a suggestion to buy certain securities. It is just my investing journal. I own all the stocks mentioned.

$HY9H.DE 10.1%
$7974 9.8%
$ORCL 9.4%

$GRAB 6.2%

$AMZN 5.5%
$BDSX 5.3%
$CIFR 5.3%
$SE 5.1%

Short positions (-94.4%)
$MTUM -27.4%
$EWT -12.0%
$ARM -4.9%
$IBIT -3.0%
$ARKG -2.7%
$AAPL -2.2%
$9434 -2.0%
$ABT -2.0%
Cash 30.5%

November has been humbling so far, and not because I got wrecked on a bunch of AI longs. In fact, I have played the regime transition very well. My view that $EWT and $MTUM had been too ahead of their skis started to pay off and the size of the index shorts was very large, so we caught a lot of spread. $ARKG also nuked, and on top of this i was short $TWST, essentially sticking with my goal of copy trading Emily Laproust, who is a great CEO but relentlessly sold the top. Being opportunisticly quite short $IBIT and also $ETHA has been quite profitable. If this weekend is anything to go off, BTC seems to have no real floor still. Maybe 50k? Which resonates with my general view that it is just kind of a failed experiment at this point. I feel much better about stuff like $HYPE, with all the equities and such coming on chain. I don’t really see what the purpose of BTC is. But i am a crypto tourist.

My large $7974/$NTDOY position (now my biggest holding!) has worked perfectly, trading as inverse memory. People have also obviously started to realize that Nintendo’s slate is extremely strong - Ocarina of Time, a remaster, has turned into a massive money printer, >5m units already. Nostalgia in the group chats, omnipresent. I used to be a video game developer, and one thing i will say is - more video games, less social media. Screen time is a plague, but many of my best memories in life have been playing video games, not mindless ones but stuff like Ocarina of Time, Starcraft, etc. Nostalgia plays. People need a break from all the anxiety in the world, and Nintendo doesn’t ask for anything from you in return.

My view is Nintendo is this generations Disney and i see no reason it can’t eventually go back to 10k+ or even ATH, once memory pricing issues subside. Until then, it will trade inverse to Hynix which is good for my portfolio.

I also opportunistically bought the dip in $CIFR, seeing that this power shell company was extremely resilient to the sell off in the AI trade (all its contracts are with Amazon and Google and are for power shell, not GPUs), and the market quickly caught up to this one. The key thing that got me into that spot was talking to some credit guys who had seen that the bonds for some of their projects were just a hair over 7%. My auto loan is higher than that and I am super nitty, have good credit, put 50% down, and am literally never defaulting. Hardly seems like this power shell with Amazon as a tenant is defaulting. I got more conviction in this theme from @origoinvest's work, which is very good and worth paying for. This one worked out quickly for +30% in a bad tape. I went decently large for a neo cloud (viewing it more like a real estate spot) although maybe if i had worked harder i could have gone a hair bigger still. It's hard when you're tired, but there definitely are spots at the moment where if you are prepared to do 8 hours work in one night, you could probably hit some fat pitches. But you don't have a week to do the work, you have one day, the market is moving extremely fast.

That’s where the positives in November end.

Though I did not get caught out like many on a reversion in the AI trade, my biggest position, $BDSX, got absolutely wrecked, down more than 50%, after they failed to meet growth targets / guidance. I still think its somewhat likely my thesis occurs (actually i think its very likely). If you’re following along, I believe Abbott Diagnostics will buy $BDSX for a variety of reasons - but like when I nailed GitLab not being dead money at $19 but ended up down small anyway (i didn’t think it was dead money at $37 either, oops - and at $32 i was just done with it), i’m afraid here i will probably not end up making enough money, even in the success scenario.

HC Wainwright and TD Cowen both maintain $34 price targets despite the bad earnings, and Jack Schuler continued to add shares despite having a huge amount, making another 1m purchase at $10.02 a couple days ago. I added a little there myself. But at this point I have a feeling Schuler would be satisfied with $24. After my adds i would make money there, but definitely not enough to compensate for the risk.

Certainly Scott Hutton, $BDSX’s CEO, would be ok with that price, as his options would pay out around 6 million there. At the age of 56, thats probably enough to just retire. At $8-10, he gets essentially nothing. At $36, its nice, but not THAT different to $24 for him. This all sounds like a bit of cope, but the company is definitely worth a value investment from Abbott, who could buy it at 2.5x gross profit ($25 a share), fire all the primary care sales people (they have their own, and this has been the main issue leading to the stalled growth), and integrate it with their overall platform. V good scenario. With the growth, its worth a lot more than that, but even with slightly lower (or no) growth, it would be net accretive immediately to Abbott at any reasonable valuation.

So, I am going to see this one through. I still think my read is dead on. I expect any acquisition to play out early next year which is optimal for the insiders (who wants to have a big gain in December?). But at this point, I am self aware enough to know that sometimes when I am certain I am right, I am still occasionally wrong. And, sometimes, you can be right and still not make enough money, which is the most likely scenario here in my view.

So… BDSX, not great.

This isn’t where it ended for small cap bio stuff. $XGN has sold off decently after earnings also, though they mostly reached guidance. My position there was much smaller, but it didn’t help performance. And a small $CADL position that i had, which had grown quite large after a 100% run up, also nuked about 25% as management pushed guidance for their BLA application out until next year. I’m mostly ok with those two although with $CADL specifically, management sold a lot at $12 in September and I really should have considered that more seriously too. I optimized for long term capital gains there (I hit the LTCG point in March) and got punished.

I think given how big the advantage was waiting until March, i am ok with my play, but it goes to show how nominal returns don’t tell the whole story for US investors. Waiting 4 months would net me 20% of a 100% gain, +defer that gain by a full year - this is a HUGE difference. But none of that shows up in the P&L.

Anyway, it’s not all bad as I said. I am positioned well for Monday, comfortably only 67% net long, with a bias to defensives, but still with enough AI exposure that I don’t really care what happens at this point, just observing and studying a lot like always.

I will head out to TomorrowXSummit Monday. If you’ll be around, feel free to DM me, maybe we can get some coffee in the hallways.
Let’s go!

Well, the pain continued going into Friday. A series of events in biotech land was actually the biggest factor strangely enough, although I did get a good win from INSM getting interest from Sanofi as an acquisition target, so, there was positive luck too.

That said, in the week,

$ABVX: short report.
$BDSX: bit of a white whale here, continued to just slowly bleed out like a stuck pig. I have been adding, my view is nothing has changed about the spot from say, $18 (i can see a rerating to 1.8x gross profit on the murkier growth scenario) to… $7.80? Which i see as just, out at any price behaviour.
$DAVE: continued selling down as a random high beta name.
$QTRX: CEO quit to go run WGS - this was a modest position but -30% still hurts. I completely cut it Friday to take the L, even though I think its possibly very asymetric here at 1x cash / well below tangible book value.
$CADL: -50% deferring their drugs BLA out to next year. I've written about this before, just unfortunate i think.
$SE / $GRAB: well positioned emerging markets companies.

The reality is just this is a correlation one sell off, justified by a truly stick situation - high oil prices as a result of a sticky Iran situation making it impossible to cut interest rates.

Unlike some who think all their stocks deserve to go up and shouldn't be affected by bad macro, i do not prescribe to this view. Bad things happen when valuations are stretched or the macro is bad. The specific event that occurs (say, Jensen leaving NVDA) always feels like a Black Swan appeared out of nowhere... but when the music stops you realize you had been listening to Tchaikovsy and it was only a matter of time.

It's not all bad - I have been absolutely printing it on shorts, now comfortably 51% long going into Monday and with the higher beta stuff selling off hard. This has left my main long short account up 77.67% YTD (despite also being where i hold the very large BDSX position, down 66%?). My LO account is up 5-7% (depending on how you count the blended value) - quite dire.

The blended amount is somewhere around 45% YTD, which i guess is good, but i would be lying if i said i didn’t feel like i fully stuck the landing here despite relentlessly aiming to. I'm not going to be too hard on myself as I feel like to some extent, my hands have been tied in my LO account. It is much easier to trade flexibly with the ability to short stocks.

And my choice of longs has been heavily defensive, with a sector bias to healthcare. But I guess i could have been around 5-10% long compute at this stage if i truly didn't believe in the spots. Deep down I still think we are in the middle of the industrial revolution for knowledge work, I think Amazon and Google have 0 problems getting enough cash to fund their part of the buildout, and being a supplier for them seems to be extremely profitable for smaller companies (say, $TTMI, maybe $CLS, etc). Anthropic just raised a huge amount of money!

The bears would laugh at this thinking, and say i have been 'trying a long' still (modestly increasing exposure expecting by the dip behaviour), a sign that I am not seeing the board clearly - i think this is a pretty reasonable view. But on the other hand, you have SanDisk at 90b market cap, buying back 5b stock last q, and with buybacks set to increase further. What is the point at which it is too good to be true? 50b? And SanDisk isn't even the best spot in the AI trade, probably not even top 5 in my view. Although it's likely Druck and co cut their buys of $STX and $WDC after Hinojosa was elected, are those companies legitimately 20-30% worse than when he sold now? I'm not so sure.

So, I think if i had to say one thing I’ve been doing poorly, it’s been trying to catch an upswing in the AI trade and then eventually bailing. And I actually think i have maybe bled a bit in the choppy market environment not being completely crystalized in my thinking. It is not really a good environment for putting on a modest feeler position after spending some time looking at the financials - better to go in with more clarity. Why? Well, you will sell during the volatility, and spreads are also wide. So you are just bleeding in the chop.

It is the time for making clear eyed investments or just not investing at all.

That is what i will be doing going into Monday. Mental clarity. What 3-4 spots do i want to have big positions in at the end of all this (eg buying oil companies when WTI is $5)? And if i was trading a market neutral or 0% long book, where would i be aiming to make money capturing spreads?

Lastly, with both longs and shorts blown out so badly, I also do need to take a look at my book from the perspective of beta - it would be good to be roughly beta neutral across longs and shorts from here, it is very easy for one side to get blown out. I am very cognizant of ending up in a situation where a big upside swing will have a sharp reversion in my short book and i will not have sufficient long exposure to 0 this out. I think at 51% net long this isn't really an issue still, but it is top of mind - and really makes you realize how delicate running at 0-10% long must be. Definitely not for amateurs, especially if your mandate lets you short software to long semis (or the opposite).
I fancy myself a bit of a soothsayer, but MediaTek limit up Sunday night was not my base case here, i'll tell you that.
